prerequisites: No prior knowledge is required. First programming skills from computer science classes are desirable.

learning_outcomes.text: Students are able to create simple procedural and object-oriented programs in a programming language under guidance. This includes the ability to identify and correct errors in programs.
Students understand the meaning, generalizability, and transferability of taught concepts (e.g., collections, polymorphism, ...).
Students can analyze simple problems and implement them into corresponding programs.
Students are able to diagnose the functioning of simple programs and describe them using appropriate technical vocabulary.

syllabus_topics: Statements (assignment, evaluation of expressions, function calls)
Concepts of imperative and procedural programming
assessment_rules: The selection of graded and ungraded examination types from the given options is at the discretion of the respective lecturer, adhering to the valid study regulations. For the graded examination (written exam), the duration is as per the valid study regulations. For ungraded experimental work, approximately 5 experiments are required in total. For regular attendance, a minimum presence of 80% of the course is required.
